lines.trans: Do not look at me like that.
Now money is more important than any silly principles.
With these winnings I will buy food.
Viktor Petrovich, what is happening in the kitchen?
Why are the dishes being prepared so slowly?
The cooks are working at the normal working pace.
Unhappy guests are already leaving the restaurant!
Let them wait a bit for their hot steaks.
The waiters cannot cope with such a flow.
I will personally go and speed up the team.
Do it right now, chef.
Everything will be ready in five minutes.
I hope you are telling the honest truth.

The waiters cannot cope with such a flow.
I will personally go and speed up the team.
Do it right now, chef.
Everything will be ready in five minutes.
I hope you are telling the honest truth.
My kitchen always maintains a high standard.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'winnings', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('gain') (profit from winning) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот это да, забери свой большой выигрыш!
examples.trans: Wow look at that, take your big winnings!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, вот ваш выигрыш, забирайте фишки.
examples.trans: Please, here is your winnings, take the chips.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'high', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'приготовиться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We are simply preparing for the morning show.
The students were preparing for the exam.
And little Grisha is preparing for the morning show.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: imperative держи! when handing something over
imperative держи! when handing something over
Secondary conversational sense ('catch!, grab (him)!') (держи его!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'team; command' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('command, order') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'feed, food (for animals)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Настя купила в магазине специальный корм для бездомных котят.
examples.trans: Nastya bought special food for stray kittens at the store.

examples.text: Для рыб в ресторанном аквариуме нужен дорогой сухой корм.
examples.trans: Expensive dry food is needed for the fish in the restaurant aquarium.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'any', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'brand, mark, stamp' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Моя кухня всегда держит высокую марку.
examples.trans: My kitchen always keeps a high standard.

examples.text: Я Марина Сергеевна. А это мои студенты.
examples.trans: I'm Marina Sergeyevna. And these are my students.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'довольный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dissatisfied, unhappy').

examples.text: Славик, ну ты вечно всем недоволен!
examples.trans: Slavik, you are always dissatisfied with everything!
I see, the landlady was very unhappy.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'stream, flow, rush' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Официанты не справляются с таким потоком.
examples.trans: The waiters cannot cope with such a flow.

examples.text: Там такие деньги! Деньги рекой потекут.
examples.trans: There's so much money in it! Money will flow like a river.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нцип'). Common masculine noun meaning 'principle' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сейчас деньги важнее любых глупых принципов.
examples.trans: Now money is more important than any silly principles.

examples.text: В принципе, вкус нормальный и не плохой.
examples.trans: In principle, the taste is fine and not bad.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('five') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'working', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('worker') (as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'правляться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cope'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Ты отлично справляешься сегодня на смене.
examples.trans: You are doing great on the shift today.

examples.text: Он легко справлялся с любой задачей.
examples.trans: He easily coped with any task.
Do not argue, Fedya managed somehow!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тейк'). Common masculine noun meaning 'steak' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пусть немного подождут свои горячие стейки.
examples.trans: Let them wait a bit for their hot steaks.

examples.text: Вот вкусный французский стейк и горячая рыба.
examples.trans: Here is a delicious French steak and hot fish.
Just like your steak from yesterday!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'pace, tempo' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Повара работают в обычном рабочем темпе.
examples.trans: The cooks are working at the normal working pace.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'скорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to speed up, accelerate', paired with 'ускорять'.

examples.text: Я лично пойду и ускорю команду.
examples.trans: I will personally go and speed up the team.

examples.text: Я сейчас лично пойду на кухню и ускорю всю команду.
examples.trans: I will personally go to the kitchen right now and speed up the whole team.

examples.text: Нам нужно срочно ускорить подачу горячих блюд для банкета.
examples.trans: We need to urgently speed up the service of hot dishes for the banquet.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Уходи отсюда скорее, пока шеф не увидел тебя без формы!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly before the chef sees you without a uniform!

meanings.note: + accusative: через неделю = in a week
Secondary conversational sense ('through, across') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean
Secondary conversational sense ('pure') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
